ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
An $ 8$-foot by $ 10$-foot floor is tiled with square tiles of size $ 1$ foot by $ 1$ foot. Each tile has a pattern consisting of four white quarter circles of radius $ 1/2$ foot centered at each corner of the tile. The remaining portion of the tile is shaded. How many square feet of the floor are shaded?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The image shows a square tile, with a white quarter-circle arc region at each of the four corners, and the arcs connect from the midpoints of adjacent sides; the remaining curved diamond-shaped region in the middle of the tile is the shaded part. Then reason: Each tile is 1 foot × 1 foot, so its area is 1 square foot. Each white part is a quarter circle with radius 1/2 foot, and the four quarter circles together equal a complete circle with radius 1/2 foot, with area π(1/2)^2 = π/4. Therefore, the shaded area of each tile is 1 - π/4. The floor size is 8 feet × 10 feet, with a total of 80 tiles of 1 square foot, so the total shaded area is 80(1 - π/4) = 80 - 20π.

method.method_draft: Compute the shaded area tile-by-tile. From the image, identify that the unshaded parts of one tile are four quarter-circles at the four corners, and the shaded part is everything else in the square. From the text, use that each tile is 1 ft by 1 ft and each quarter-circle has radius 1/2 ft. The area of one tile is 1 square foot. The total white area in one tile is 4 times a quarter-circle of radius 1/2, which equals one full circle of radius 1/2: pi(1/2)^2 = pi/4. Thus the shaded area per tile is 1 - pi/4. The floor has 8*10 = 80 tiles, so multiply: 80(1 - pi/4) = 80 - 20pi.

method.method_draft: Compute the whole floor area first, then subtract the total white area by grouping quarter-circles across the tiling. From the image, observe that quarter-circles at adjacent tile corners meet around grid vertices: four quarters around an interior vertex form one full circle of radius 1/2, two quarters along an edge vertex form a half-circle, and one quarter appears at each floor corner. From the text, the floor is tiled by 8 by 10 unit tiles, so its area is 80 square feet and its grid of tile vertices is 9 by 11. Count vertex types: interior vertices are 7*9 = 63, edge non-corner vertices are 2*7 + 2*9 = 32, and floor corner vertices are 4. The total white area is equivalent to 63 full circles plus 32 half-circles plus 4 quarter-circles, all of radius 1/2. This is 63 + 16 + 1 = 80 full-circle equivalents of radius 1/2, so white area is 80*pi(1/2)^2 = 20pi. Therefore shaded area is total area minus white area: 80 - 20pi.
